title: Profound vs Peec AI (2026): Pricing, Engines, Content
summary: Profound vs Peec AI compared for 2026: published vs quoted pricing, engines tracked, data depth, content Agents, and a self-serve option that fixes the gap.
body_markdown:
**Profound and Peec AI are the two most-searched AEO tools of 2026, and they are built for different buyers.** Profound is an enterprise platform with the deepest data in the category and Agents that now write and publish; you buy it through a demo. Peec is a clean, self-serve tracker from $95 a month that measures beautifully and, by design, writes nothing.


## The short answer


- **Pick Profound** if you are an enterprise brand that needs nine engines, prompt demand data, SSO and SOC 2, and has the budget for a custom contract.
- **Pick Peec** if you are an SEO team with writers who needs affordable, trustworthy tracking and will do the fixing yourselves.
- **Pick neither** if you want the pages written and published without an enterprise contract.[Sprites](https://www.sprites.ai/ai-visibility-tracking) does that, and is free to start.

## Pricing: published vs quoted


This is the sharpest difference. Peec publishes every self-serve price and bills on prompts, with three models and unlimited seats on every plan. Profound retired its $99 Starter and $399 Growth plans; today its page lists a free seven-day trial of 50 prompts on ChatGPT, Gemini and AI Overviews, and a custom Enterprise plan. A team that needs a number for a budget line this week can get one from Peec and cannot get one from Profound.


## Data depth


Profound goes deeper. Prompt Volumes gives real-conversation demand data, Agent Analytics reads AI crawler traffic through Cloudflare, Vercel, Fastly and others, and ChatGPT Shopping tracks product answers. Peec covers the core metrics very well, visibility, position, sentiment, share of voice, citation sources and query fan-outs, and added AI Shopping and Brand Perception in 2026. For most mid-market decisions, Peec’s data is enough; for enterprise planning across markets, Profound’s is richer.


## What happens after the dashboard


Here the two have split. Profound’s Agents research, draft and publish FAQ pages, page refreshes and new articles to WordPress, Sanity and Contentful, orchestrated by Aim, a background agent launched in July 2026. Peec stops at recommended actions and says so on its own site. If you buy Peec, budget for the writer.


The AEO category as one pipeline. The question for every tool is where its bar stops, and what you do by hand after that.

## Profound vs Peec: frequently asked questions


### Profound vs Peec AI: which is better?


Profound is better for enterprise brands that need up to nine engines, real-conversation prompt demand data, SSO, SOC 2 and Agents that publish content. Peec AI is better for SEO teams that want clean, affordable tracking with unlimited seats and published prices from $95 a month. Neither runs paid ads; Sprites covers tracking, writing, publishing and ads in one self-serve plan.


### Is Peec AI cheaper than Profound?


Yes, and it is the only one of the two with published self-serve prices: $95, $245 and $495 a month. Profound offers a free seven-day trial and then a custom Enterprise contract through a demo; its old $99 and $399 plans are no longer on its pricing page.


### Which tracks more AI engines, Profound or Peec?


Profound tracks up to nine engines on Enterprise, including ChatGPT, Perplexity, Google AI Mode and AI Overviews, Gemini, Copilot, Claude, DeepSeek and Exa. Peec’s self-serve plans track three models of your choice, with more as add-ons, and its Enterprise plan tracks up to 13.


### Does Profound or Peec create content?


Profound does: its Agents research, draft and publish to WordPress, Sanity and Contentful, on Enterprise contracts. Peec does not, by design; it recommends actions and leaves writing to your team. Sprites writes and publishes on self-serve plans, and is free to start.
